rows.title: NFL wind: four Sunday totals to verify
rows.observation: The November 1 source selections are NE–MIA under 43.5 (-113), LAC–LAR under 45.5 (-111), ATL–TB under 43.5 (-111), and IND–JAX under 46.5 (-110). The screen uses average wind of at least 10 mph and temperatures from 33 to 90 degrees; displayed history is 635-467-10 with 11% ROI.
rows.interpretation: WATCH: these are source claims, not verified game-time weather effects. Stadium shelter and roof conditions can invalidate an outdoor weather proxy. Historical ROI is not a forecast for these four games.
rows.next_check: Verify venue, roof/open-air exposure and forecast near kickoff; compare the exact current total and price. Re-capture tomorrow before a new decision. No automatic wind adjustment.
rows.quote_status: Source-pick benchmark only; no verified executable sportsbook quote

rows.title: Portland–Utah: investigate the under
rows.observation: Action lists Under 232.5 at -112 as a system selection for October 31. Its displayed history is 534 wins, 434 losses, 9 pushes and 7% ROI. Filters include division games in the regular season, under support at 40% or less, and a total falling by at least one point from open to close.
rows.interpretation: WATCH: closing-line information is unavailable when an earlier ticket is placed. This is a third-party historical screen, not our calibrated win probability. The discovery row and expanded chart also disagree on total units; those units are not used.
rows.next_check: Compare the same sportsbook total at the actual decision time, verify line movement and current injuries/pace, then track an independent forward benchmark. Do not apply a fixed probability boost or copy the source stake.

rows.title: System discovery: win rate alone can mislead
rows.observation: The catalog includes both winning and losing historical screens. Its college-football Sharp Money screen shows 51% wins and -1% ROI; an MLB public-fade moneyline screen shows 59% wins and -3% ROI.
rows.interpretation: Use price-adjusted returns, sample size and forward results; neither a sharp-money label nor a high hit rate proves value. Selecting only the best historical screens risks selection bias.
rows.next_check: Keep source systems separate from agency results; test rules prospectively with timestamped inputs and realistic prices before changing betting behavior.
rows.quote_status: Source-pick benchmark only; no verified executable sportsbook quote

rows.title: College football: compare external model disagreements
rows.observation: At capture the dashboard displayed South Alabama +6.5 versus projection +2, Air Force +0.5 versus -3.5, and Kansas State +2.5 versus -1.2 for October 31 matchups. These are external model comparison leads, not accepted picks or verified book offers.
rows.interpretation: WATCH: a forecast disagreement identifies something to investigate. It does not establish which model is right. The dashboard supplies no named executable sportsbook for these displayed offers.
rows.next_check: Resolve full team/event identities and current sportsbook contracts, compare our forecast and injuries, and preserve the disagreement for later outcome scoring.

evidence_decisions.note: New paper evaluations use supported fresh evidence. CFBD quality-screen v1 is active for CFB moneylines and laying-points spreads: a joint offensive/defensive disadvantage with four-game samples raises required edge by 2 percentage points and caps stakes at one unit. It can change takes to passes without changing forecast probabilities. Totals and underdog spreads retain existing rules. Experimental, not proven profitable. Injury scenarios can change NBA prop forecasts (maximum 5 percentage points; half-unit stake cap). Falling minutes and matched moneyline crowding can raise required edge. Verified AI caution/reject assessments can tighten or hold a decision; narrative summaries cannot set probabilities. These hypotheses are not proven profitable. Counterpoint keeps its separate inverse experiment; NFL prop holds remain.
limitations: No unattended Action Network collection; snapshots expire after 30 minutes
Spread/total splits need exact source-line identity and remain display-only
Missing evidence retains the original forecast and is explicitly recorded
Existing tickets are never reselected or rewritten

decision_policy.note: Active experimental paper rule: for moneylines and spreads laying points (including pick-em), if the selected team has at least 0.05 lower offensive PPA/play AND at least 0.05 higher defensive PPA allowed than its opponent, require 2 additional percentage points of model edge and cap the stake at one unit. This is an unvalidated selection screen, not a calibrated probability model. Counterpoint keeps its inverse experiment.

claude_reviews.summary: Top observations (review-only; no code run; saved tests belong to a different source snapshot, so no test evidence applies). 1) Definite accounting/identity concern, sportsbook.py:194-206: selection picks max(edge-threshold) across books/sides, but 'edge' for CFB/injury paths is computed from d['probability'], while the stake formula at line 201 and the pass/accept test at 206 compare edge to decision['threshold'] of the chosen quote only; a blocked quote can still be selected when no eligible option exists (eligible or options) and is then marked 'pass' correctly, but 'changed' (line 197) compares against original_q chosen by raw edge, so selection_changed can be reported true purely from tie-breaking on book name. 2) Temporal/staleness: evidence_decisions.py:54 filters splits by captured_utc freshness (<=0.5h) but allows captured_utc in the future relative to now (fresh() permits only past via timedelta(0)<=...; splits path uses the same fn, OK), whereas evidence_decisions.py:31-34 reads rows keyed on created_utc but never checks the news/trend game tip vs now; and line 122 'last_history_date < now.date()' uses UTC date, which can admit same-local-day history. Context.signature (line 71-73) includes self.ai dicts directly, so any AI text change re-triggers fresh decisions each tick: unbounded sb_decisions growth is plausible (hypothesis, not verified). 3) Calibration/double-adjustment: sportsbook.py:132 adds a fixed bias to probabilities, then evidence blends (evidence_decisions.py:133) off the already-biased prior; the 5pp cap and fixed weights (lines 11-12) are explicitly uncalibrated, and normal-error sigma values (sportsbook.py:125) are assumptions, so reported 'edge' is not a validated advantage. Also grade() pushes on quarter-lines are filtered at load (line 58) but Asian-handicap quotes via site_odds/mlb loaders bypass that filter (line 70-76), a possible settlement error.

1) Possible temporal/staleness gap (hypothesis, needs verification): shared_research_service.py:66 admits news hypotheses to deliveries on tip_utc>now only. Freshness gating happens in evaluate() at line 25 via source captured_utc within 4h, but the research context notes Banchero's 'out' report is old despite fresh capture/quotes; evaluate() checks capture time and quote time but not the report's own publication time, so an old injury report with a fresh capture could pass as SHADOW_CANDIDATE. 2) Possible double-adjustment/identity risk: information_intake.py:47 keys rows by identity(p) in a dict, so same-identity files silently overwrite each other (last sorted wins) without conflict reporting, and load() reads only the last 200 sorted files at line 44 (silent truncation by filename date). Separately, information_intake.py:124 candidate() matches targets on game_key plus tip, but at line 127 sport-only context (no target) is attached to every game in the sport; affects_betting=False limits harm but exposes a potential for downstream double-counting of CFB EPA if later adapters read it (shared_research_service.py:118-123 already notes no second boost; unverified). 3) Accounting/integrity: shared_research_service.py:93-98 inserts deliveries with INSERT OR IGNORE keyed by digest of content that includes counts but evaluate uses the injected 'now' in gating; record() is called only when inserted, which is good, but tick() at line 148-150 wraps in a transaction while earlier steps (market_context deliver, line 141) commit outside it, so a failure at delivery leaves partial state. Tests are for a different source snapshot, so no quality or correctness certification; rerun before approval.

1) Definite risk (cfbd_ppa.py:100-113, 117): attach() trusts the CFBD row 'season'/'week'/'gameId' and matches only the schedule row; the history filter relies on s['week'] from ESPN, but the CFBD 'week' field for each prior game is never compared to p['before_week'] using the CFBD row itself (line 117 uses int(r['week']), which is equal to the schedule week by line 109, so OK) -- however the cutoff uses week only, not kickoff time, so same-week-numbered or bye/postseason-shifted games and 'seasonType' filters are untested; cfb_efficiency.py:80-81 does add a kickoff<tip guard but cfbd_ppa.py:117 does not, so CFBD history lacks the equivalent temporal check (hypothesis: low practical leakage because only finals >6h old are accepted, but asymmetric). 2) Identity weakness (cfbd_ppa.py:89-111): school() uses longest normalized prefix match of the full ESPN name against CFBD school names; names like 'Miami (OH)'/'Miami', 'San Jose State', or mascot-suffix collisions could resolve to the wrong school, and a wrong-but-consistent match passes the {team,opponent}=={h,a} check only if both rows agree, so risk is modest but unvalidated. 3) Policy/calibration (cfb_efficiency.py:179-213): the 0.05 PPA/play thresholds and +2pp edge are untuned, unvalidated and applied on equal-game, non-opponent-adjusted averages with a 4-game minimum (very noisy early season); the threshold is raised via max() on out['threshold'] but the 'cap stake at one unit' claimed in POLICY/reason is not enforced in this function (no stake cap set here), so it may be a documentation/behavior mismatch needing verification in the caller. Also fetch() reserves the daily file before the request, so a transient failure locks out the endpoint for the UTC day (cfbd_ppa.py:41-44), and load() takes the lexicographically last file regardless of status. Saved tests are stale, so nothing here is certified.

bankroll_policy: New paper stakes: at most 40% committed overall, 10% per sport, 2% per game and 1% per ticket. At most 10% committed beyond 24 hours. Sportsbook NBA/NFL game lines may use 7.5% per sport, leaving 2.5% of bankroll for props within the 10% sport limit. Percentages use the lower of initial bankroll and current cash plus open stakes; profits do not automatically increase limits. Existing locked tickets remain intact, and may exceed new limits until settlement. Model and sportsbook accounts stay separate.
